faq: Do I need Adobe Commerce for B2B?

Not always. Customer groups, tier prices and minimum quantities work on Open Source. Shared catalogs and built-in quotes are Adobe Commerce features. We tell you which route fits and what any paid extension costs.
Can one Magento install run several stores?

Yes. Magento supports multiple websites, stores and store views from one admin, each with its own language, currency and catalog rules. We set up the structure that matches how you sell and keep it simple.
Will custom checkout changes break updates?
We use layout XML, plugins and extensions the Magento way and avoid editing core files, so upgrades stay possible. We note each change, and test cart, shipping and payment after it.
Can you set per-country tax rules?
We configure the tax classes and rules you provide in Magento's tax tools. We do not give tax advice, so please confirm the rates and rules with your accountant before we set them.
desc:
A Magento multi-store and B2B setup lets one installation serve several languages, countries and buyer types, each with the right prices and checkout rules. Ecom Swift LLC plans, builds and tests that structure in your own Magento store, so a larger catalog stays easy to run.

## What is a Magento multi-store and B2B setup?

A Magento multi-store and B2B setup is a way of arranging one Magento installation so it can present different storefronts and different prices to different groups of buyers. Store views carry the language, currency and labels for each market. Customer groups carry the special pricing, tax treatment and ordering rules for each type of buyer, such as retail shoppers, wholesale accounts or distributors.

The result is a single catalog and a single admin that behaves like several shops. You edit a product once and each store view shows it in the right form.

## Why larger catalogs need a planned structure

Magento gives you many ways to build the same thing, and the wrong choice is hard to reverse once orders and customers are attached to it. A second language added as a copy of the whole store doubles your upkeep. A wholesale price list typed into product pages by hand drifts out of date within a month. Tax settings applied to the wrong scope produce invoices your accountant has to correct.

Planning before building avoids this. We decide which settings belong at the website level, which at the store level and which at the store view level, so changes later touch one place instead of five.

## How the setup affects revenue and workload

Buyers purchase more easily when the store speaks their language, shows their currency and charges the tax that applies to them. A trade customer who sees their negotiated price after login does not need to phone you for a quote. A business that must order in cases of twelve gets a clear message instead of a failed cart.

The same structure cuts internal work. Fewer manual price edits, fewer support questions about totals and fewer corrections after an order means your team spends time on selling. Results still depend on your catalog, your traffic and your market, so we describe what the setup removes from the buyer's way, not a sales number.

## What a well-built advanced Magento setup includes

- Store views mapped to each language or country, with a clear parent website and store structure.
- Currency and locale settings, including display formats and rounding rules per store view.
- Translated labels for navigation, product page text, cart and checkout messages.
- Customer groups with their own prices, set through tier prices or catalog price rules.
- Shared catalogs or category permissions where your edition supports them.
- Minimum order amounts and quantity rules, with messages that explain the limit.
- A quote request flow, so buyers can ask for a price on larger orders.
- Checkout changes such as extra fields, a trimmed step or a purchase order number.
- Tax classes and rates assigned per store, with test orders that confirm the totals.
- A written setup note so your team knows where every rule lives.

## How we build it

We start with a short planning step. You tell us which markets and buyer types you serve, and we sketch the website, store and store view layout for your approval. Nothing is built until that plan makes sense to you.

We then build on a staging copy. Each store view, customer group and rule is created, and we place test orders as a retail buyer, a trade buyer and a guest to check prices, tax and shipping. Only after the results match the plan do we move the changes to your live store, with a backup taken first.

The Basic package covers one extra store view with its language and currency. The Standard package adds customer groups, pricing rules, order limits and one checkout change. The Premium package combines several store views, shared catalogs, a quote flow, custom checkout fields and per-store tax in one build.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- List every market and buyer type before the build starts.
- Decide who sets wholesale prices and how often they change.
- Keep product data clean, because every store view reads from it.
- Test with real example orders, including a refund.
- Keep custom checkout changes small and documented.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a separate Magento install for every country.
- Typing special prices into individual products when a rule would do.
- Hiding minimum order rules until the cart page.
- Changing tax settings on the live store without a test order.
- Stacking many checkout extensions that edit the same step.

## Who it is for

This service suits a retailer who is adding a second country and needs translated pages, local currency and local tax. It also suits a wholesaler who wants trade customers to log in and see their own prices and order limits. A growing brand that sells to both shoppers and businesses from one catalog is a third common case.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your markets, buyer types and any price lists you already use, plus your translations or the languages you need. We also need collaborator, staff or developer access to your Magento admin and hosting, given as a separate user. We never ask for passwords, and we work only in your own account.
